<!--
Used by humans via this template, and by the monthly doc-structure audit
(.github/workflows/doc-structure.yml), which writes the same sections via
`gh issue create --body`.

Restructure issues are rejected or stall for one reason above all others: the
reader impact is asserted rather than shown, so nobody can weigh the change
against the churn. Fill in "Why it matters" properly or expect the issue to sit.
-->

## Current structure

<!-- The navigation path, exactly as `scripts/audit_navigation.py` reports it. -->

```
Documentation > Tutorials > Evaluation
```

**Pages affected:**

<!-- Page paths as they appear in config/navigation.json. -->

- `tutorials/evaluate_trails_with_opa`

## What's wrong

<!--
Name the finding kind if it came from the audit: single-child group, deep
nesting, Title Case label, oversized group, inconsistent icons. Otherwise
describe it plainly.
-->

## Why it matters

<!--
Reader impact, not tidiness. Who is looking for these pages, and what does the
current shape cost them — an extra click, a wrong guess, two places to look for
one topic, a label that promises something the contents don't deliver?

A finding with no reader impact is not worth the churn of moving pages. Say so
and close it instead.
-->

## Proposed structure

```
Documentation > Tutorials
  └─ tutorials/evaluate_trails_with_opa
```

## URL impact

<!--
Get this right — it is the part most often missed, and the part that breaks
things for people outside this repo.

- Renaming a GROUP LABEL      → no URL change. Nothing else to do.
- Re-ordering within a group   → no URL change.
- Collapsing a group wrapper   → no URL change IF the page file does not move.
- MOVING OR RENAMING A PAGE FILE → the URL changes. Requires a
  `config/redirects.json` entry, because the old URL is in customers'
  bookmarks, in CLI error output, and in changelog entries.

Also check anchors: if a heading is being renamed, grep for its anchor first.
Some are referenced from outside this repo — the CLI prints
`faq/faq#boolean-flags` in an error message.
-->

- [ ] No page files move — nav-only change, no redirects needed
- [ ] Page files move — redirects required, listed below

<!-- If pages move, list old path → new path: -->

## Out of scope

<!--
Navigation subtrees that are generated must not be restructured by hand:

- `Reference > CLI Reference` — generated by `scripts/update-cli-nav.py` from
  the CLI's command tree. A single-child `kosli allow` group reflects that the
  command has one subcommand. Change the generator, or upstream in
  `kosli-dev/cli`, never navigation.json.
- `helm/k8s_reporter/*`, `client_reference/kosli*` — page content is generated.
  Re-homing them in navigation is fine; editing them is not.

Confirm this proposal does not touch generated structure.
-->

## Evidence

<!-- The command that found it, and its relevant output. -->

```
$ python3 scripts/audit_navigation.py --json
```

## Verification

- [ ] `python3 scripts/audit_navigation.py --check` — integrity still clean
- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/` — navigation integrity test passes
- [ ] `mint broken-links` — no new broken links
- [ ] Redirects added for every moved page, and the old URLs resolve
